notes: The apostles write to slaves and to masters in a world where slavery was normal. They do not call for its abolition, and they say that in Christ master and slave are brothers. Philemon is the clearest case.
Paul greets women as co-workers and a deacon (Phoebe), and in other places asks women to be silent in the assembly. Mary Magdalene is the first to see the risen Lord.
Paul commends celibacy; 1 Timothy 3:2 says an overseer should be the husband of one wife; Peter had a wife.
These passages describe who Christ commissioned at the Last Supper and after the Resurrection, and the qualities of the early overseers.
The rich young man, the rich man and Lazarus, the first Christians holding things in common, and James's warning to the rich are the passages most often cited.
